X.note: Matted painting with a slight 3D tilt and a warm vignette. The red damask against the dark brown ground gives good colour contrast. The caption gradient overlaps the lower part of the mat and the painting, so it dirties them. The credit line is small, low-contrast grey and will be hard to read on a phone. The caption sits far from the subject, and the gap between title and credit is wasted space. The overall look is a photo pasted on a tilted card, not a lit 3D scene.

Y.note: Same template. The sepia photo is well framed and the full-figure subject reads cleanly. The negative has a ragged torn edge at upper right, which adds some authenticity. The caption and gradient cover the lower part of the photo and mat, and the credit line is small and dim. The tilted card has no real depth, shadow or lighting, so it still looks flat.

why: Both frames use an identical template with the same strengths (clear subject, clear name and date) and the same weaknesses (tiny low-contrast credit, caption gradient muddying the image, flat card with no real lighting); Y's full-figure photo is marginally more dynamic and X's painting has richer colour.
top_fix_for_weaker: Neither is clearly weaker. For both frames: move the caption off the artwork into a clean lower-third bar, or end the artwork above it, enlarge the credit line to at least 70% of the title size with higher contrast, and add real depth to the card with a drop shadow, a soft key light and a slow parallax push-in.
